reference: GNU coreutils expr, invoked from the system Bash side of the harness with the same quoted arguments. The availability/help case checks Bash's documented builtin metadata independently.
coverage: Bash reports expr as a builtin and its help entry is available.
Integer arithmetic precedence, parentheses, truncating division, and signed remainder.
Numeric comparison, including a pair whose numeric and lexical order differ.
length, substr, and index string functions with deterministic ASCII inputs.
BRE capture output and the rule that a match must begin at the start of the subject.
Truth-value exit status, lazy OR/AND evaluation, and empty substring boundaries.
A non-integer arithmetic error with status and diagnostic presence checked.
exclusions: This is a selected GNU expr surface, not complete CLI or POSIX conformance.
Only the runner's fixed C locale is covered; multibyte and locale-sensitive behavior is not covered.
Large integer overflow, GNU-only extensions, and pathological regular-expression guard cases are outside this bounded suite.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash identifies expr as a builtin and can resolve its help entry; metadata is separate from operation coverage.
cases.script: type -t expr; IFS= read -r help_line < <(help expr); [[ $help_line == 'expr: Evaluate POSIX expr(1) expressions' ]]; printf '%s\n' "$help_line"
cases.stdout:
builtin
expr: Evaluate POSIX expr(1) expressions

cases.purpose: Check multiplication precedence, parenthesized grouping, truncation toward zero, and signed remainder on small integers.
Check that two integer operands compare numerically: 10 is not less than 2, despite their lexical order.
Check the three common string operators and their 1-based indexing on ASCII input.
cases.script: expr length abcdef; expr substr abcdef 2 3; expr index abcdef cfz

cases.purpose: Check POSIX BRE matching with a parenthesized capture, which returns the first captured text rather than the match length.
Check that expr's colon operator does not search later in the string when the BRE has no match at the beginning.
Check that a truthy left operand is returned and a skipped division-by-zero branch does not raise an error.
Check that a false left operand yields zero and skips division by zero on the right.
Check the POSIX out-of-range substring result: an empty string is printed and the expression status is false.
Check GNU expr's error status and presence of a diagnostic for invalid arithmetic operands without pinning wording.
Evaluated division by zero reports GNU error status 2 with diagnostics.
Lazy evaluation still parses a skipped branch and rejects its missing operand.
A successful empty BRE capture prints a newline and has false status.
